observations: Two black power banks held together with tape.
One unit is wrapped in light-colored masking tape.
One unit is wrapped in black electrical tape.
Braided USB cables (green and blue) are connected or adjacent.
No brand names, model numbers, or capacity markings are visible in the photo.
The casing appears to be DIY or heavily damaged.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows units held together with tape and in poor physical condition.
The internal cells are not visible.
Requires a time-lapse or discharge test.
The use of tape to hold the casings together strongly suggests they have been opened or the original housing failed.

risks.risk: Fire or explosion hazard due to DIY assembly
risks.proof: Video of the device charging and discharging under load without overheating.
Photo of a USB capacity tester showing total mAh delivered.
Close-up photo of the USB ports.

proof_requests: Photo of the internal battery cells.
Video of the devices successfully charging a mobile phone.
response.reason: The items are identified as scrap power banks. Given the tape and lack of branding, they are priced at the worst-case scenario as non-functional scrap for parts.
